title: Epsilon Indi B

catalog.source: Gaia DR3 6412596012146801152 (RUWE 4.30: astrometric binary, treat errors as optimistic)

catalog_comparison.source: Gaia DR3 6412596012146801152 (RUWE 4.30: astrometric binary, treat errors as optimistic)

spectrum.method: Forced ePSF photometry on native pixels at the motion-corrected (followed) position in every exposure; wavelength from the spectral WCS at that pixel; inverse-variance means in the 102 SPHEREx/SPIFF bins.

wing_attempt.summary: Experimental wing photometry was attempted on 1 saturated exposures; 1 had enough unflagged pixels to fit, but the release ePSF describes the wings poorly (median reduced chi-square 5), so 1 passed the acceptance cut.

fixed_vs_follow.note: Measured at one fixed sky position, the source keeps 55% of the flux recovered by following its motion (median over 99 bins).

templates.library: SPIFF SPHEREx templates (Gagné et al. 2026; M4–Y0 field, low-gravity and subdwarf grids)
templates.reason: Best template T3 (field) with reduced chi-square 1.55 over 85 bins.

naive.description: Every exposure in time order, regardless of wavelength. Because SPHEREx sees a different wavelength in each exposure, most of this apparent change is the source spectrum, not time variability.
naive.max_ratio_basis: brightest / faintest exposure among those with S/N >= 10

matched.description: Flux in the same SPHEREx wavelength bin compared between visits. Only this comparison can reveal true time variability.

hypotheses.name: Stationary astronomical source
evidence: A stationary model is rejected: delta chi-square 85772 (about 99 sigma if the per-point errors are realistic).

hypotheses.name: Moving astronomical source
evidence: Proper motion 4635 ± 16 mas/yr from 434 exposures over 526 days; model reduced chi-square 0.89.
Parallax 298 ± 9 mas measured from SPHEREx alone.

hypotheses.name: Blended or overlapping sources
evidence: Epsilon Indi Ba (T1) and Bb (T6) are separated by well under one SPHEREx pixel; the measurement is their combined light.

hypotheses.name: Instrumental or processing artifact
evidence: Detected in 434 independent exposures across 4 visits, on multiple detectors and wavelengths.

hypotheses.name: Known solar-system object
evidence: Positions over 526 days follow proper motion plus annual parallax of a few arcsec per year (reduced chi-square 0.89); solar-system bodies move arcseconds to arcminutes per hour and would not repeat a stellar track across visits.

verdicts.label: Spectrum consistent with an ultracool dwarf (T3)

summary.headline: Moves 4.63″/yr across 434 SPHEREx exposures; spectrum matches a T3 template.
summary.one_liner: Detected in 434 independent exposures with a coherent position change. The motion-corrected spectrum is consistent with a T3 template (reduced chi-square 1.5), which supports but does not prove an ultracool-dwarf classification. Nearby sources may contribute light within the 6.15-arcsec pixels.

limitations: SPHEREx pixels are 6.15 arcsec; sources closer than about 1 pixel are measured as one blend.
Positions are registered to Gaia DR3 field stars with a pure shift per exposure; residual distortion is absorbed into an empirical error floor.
Fluxes use the median pixel solid angle (OMEGA_MEDIAN) and the release ePSF; absolute calibration uncertainties of a few percent are not propagated.
A template match constrains spectral type only; it does not establish mass, age or formation history.
Ba (T1) and Bb (T6) are separated by well under one 6.15" SPHEREx pixel; PARALLAX measures the combined light.
Epsilon Indi A (Gaia DR3 6412595290592307840, G = 4.3) lies about 7 arcmin away and is outside the default 10 arcmin field.
follow_up: Check higher-resolution imaging (e.g. unWISE, 2MASS, Gaia) to separate contributors.
Extend the baseline with archival WISE/NEOWISE epochs to tighten proper motion and parallax.
